title: Managing cost and latency

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Managing cost and latency

children.text: Cost is prompt design, model choice, and how often you call. Measure per-request tokens before you try to optimise anything.
What this lesson covers
Attribute spend to specific calls and prompts
Trim prompts and route by difficulty
Set timeouts and fall back gracefully
This lesson sits in Shipping to Production, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Attribute spend to specific calls and prompts
Trim prompts and route by difficulty
Set timeouts and fall back gracefully

title: Caching and rate limits

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Caching and rate limits

children.text: Repeated prefixes can be cached, repeated questions can be answered from your own cache, and rate limits will find you eventually — so retry with backoff.
What this lesson covers
Cache stable prompt prefixes to cut cost
Retry with exponential backoff on rate limits
Queue or shed load instead of failing hard
This lesson sits in Shipping to Production, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Cache stable prompt prefixes to cut cost
Retry with exponential backoff on rate limits
Queue or shed load instead of failing hard

title: What an embedding actually encodes

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for What an embedding actually encodes

children.text: An embedding maps text to a point in space where nearby means related. It captures topic and usage, not truth, and definitely not recency.
What this lesson covers
Read an embedding as a position in semantic space
Know what embeddings fail to capture
Choose an embedding model for your content
This lesson sits in Embeddings and Vector Search, part of Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Scratch. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Read an embedding as a position in semantic space
Know what embeddings fail to capture
Choose an embedding model for your content

title: Vector databases and indexes

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Vector databases and indexes

children.text: Exact nearest-neighbour search does not scale, so vector indexes trade a little recall for a lot of speed. Knowing the trade-off keeps you out of trouble.
What this lesson covers
Understand approximate nearest neighbour search
Trade recall against latency deliberately
Store metadata alongside vectors for filtering
This lesson sits in Embeddings and Vector Search, part of Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Scratch. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Understand approximate nearest neighbour search
Trade recall against latency deliberately
Store metadata alongside vectors for filtering

title: Similarity metrics and thresholds

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Similarity metrics and thresholds

children.text: Cosine similarity is the usual default, but the number it gives you is only meaningful relative to your own corpus. Calibrate the threshold, do not guess it.
What this lesson covers
Compare cosine, dot product, and euclidean distance
Calibrate a relevance threshold on real queries
Detect the case where nothing is actually relevant
This lesson sits in Embeddings and Vector Search, part of Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Scratch. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Compare cosine, dot product, and euclidean distance
Calibrate a relevance threshold on real queries
Detect the case where nothing is actually relevant
proTip: A similarity score has no absolute meaning. Calibrate the cutoff against queries you know the answers to.

title: Chunking strategies

children.text: Chunk size decides what a match can even mean. Too small and passages lose context; too large and the relevant sentence gets drowned.
What this lesson covers
Split on structure rather than a fixed character count
Use overlap to avoid cutting an idea in half
Keep each chunk understandable on its own
This lesson sits in Ingestion and Indexing, part of Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Scratch. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Split on structure rather than a fixed character count
Use overlap to avoid cutting an idea in half
Keep each chunk understandable on its own

title: Metadata and filtered retrieval

children.text: Metadata turns semantic search into scoped semantic search. Filtering by source, type, or date removes whole classes of wrong answer.

Use metadata to attribute answers back to a source

title: Keeping the index fresh

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Keeping the index fresh

children.text: Content changes and stale chunks keep getting retrieved. Incremental reindexing driven by content events beats rebuilding everything nightly.
What this lesson covers
Reindex incrementally on content change events
Delete chunks whose source no longer exists
Version the index so a bad run can be rolled back

Delete chunks whose source no longer exists
Version the index so a bad run can be rolled back

title: Hybrid keyword and vector search

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Hybrid keyword and vector search

children.text: Vector search misses exact identifiers; keyword search misses paraphrase. Running both and fusing the rankings covers each one’s blind spot.
What this lesson covers
Combine lexical and semantic result sets
Fuse rankings rather than concatenating them
Fall back to keyword search when embeddings are unavailable
This lesson sits in Retrieval Quality, part of Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Scratch. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Combine lexical and semantic result sets
Fuse rankings rather than concatenating them
Fall back to keyword search when embeddings are unavailable
proTip: If embeddings are switched off in your environment, wildcarded keyword matching is the fallback that still works.
